exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: 59 consecutive women with isolated thrombocytopenia experiencing 63 pregnancies, who attended a single referral center over 3 years.
finding: Platelet count trends and mean platelet volume are helpful diagnostic tools for differentiating types of isolated thrombocytopenia in pregnancy; misdiagnosis can lead to unnecessary therapy and side effects, and the bleeding risk for mothers and newborns with thrombocytopenia (excluding inherited platelet function disorders) is similar to the general population.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery is associated with a lower risk of bleeding than cesarean section and is therefore preferable whenever obstetrical-gynecological conditions permit.
